chapterTitle: Chapter 5: The Halogens and Noble Gases (Group VII-A & VIII-A)
title: Chapter 5: The Halogens and Noble Gases (Group VII-A & VIII-A)
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: Which of the following halogens is the most powerful oxidizing agent?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest standard reduction potential (+2.87 V) due to low F-F bond dissociation energy and exceptionally high hydration energy of F⁻.

questions.question: The acidic strength of halogen hydracids increases in the order:
questions.explanation: Bond length increases and H-X bond dissociation energy decreases down the group (H-F = 567 kJ/mol, H-I = 299 kJ/mol), releasing H⁺ most easily in HI.

questions.question: Why does hydrofluoric acid (HF) have an anomalously high boiling point (19.5°C) compared to HCl (-85°C)?

options.B: Strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding forms zigzag (HF)_n polymer chains

questions.explanation: Fluorine's extreme electronegativity creates powerful intermolecular H-F···H hydrogen bonds requiring substantial thermal energy to break.

questions.question: Bleaching powder is manufactured industrially by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime in:
questions.explanation: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ xrightarrow{Hasenclever plant, <40°C} CaOCl₂ · H₂O (bleaching powder).

questions.question: The available chlorine in good quality bleaching powder is approximately:
questions.explanation: Commercial bleaching powder yields around 35% to 40% active available chlorine upon acidification.

questions.question: Which of the following oxyacids of chlorine is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: In HClO₄, chlorine is in the +7 oxidation state with three terminal oxo atoms stabilizing the perchlorate anion (ClO₄⁻) via extensive resonance delocalization.

questions.question: What is the molecular geometry of Xenon tetrafluoride (XeF₄) according to VSEPR theory?
questions.explanation: Xe has 8 valence electrons; bonding to 4 fluorines leaves 2 lone pairs. With an octahedral arrangement (sp³d²), the lone pairs occupy axial positions, yielding square planar geometry.

questions.question: Which noble gas is used in weather observation balloons and deep-sea diving gas cylinders (heliox)?
questions.explanation: Helium is non-flammable, exceptionally light, and has very low solubility in human blood, preventing the painful 'bends' (decompression sickness).

questions.question: Which noble gas is radioactive, produced as a daughter decay product of Radium-226?
questions.explanation: Radon-222 is an alpha-emitting noble gas resulting from the radioactive decay of Ra-226 in rock and soil.

questions.question: When hot concentrated sodium hydroxide solution reacts with chlorine gas, the products formed are:
questions.explanation: 6 NaOH (hot conc.) + 3 Cl₂ → 5 NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3 H₂O (disproportionation of Cl₂ from 0 to -1 and +5).

questions.question: What is the shape of Xenon difluoride (XeF₂) according to VSEPR theory?
questions.explanation: XeF₂ has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs (sp³d). The 3 lone pairs occupy equatorial positions at 120°, forcing the two F atoms into axial positions at 180° (linear).

questions.question: Which interhalogen compound has a pentagonal bipyramidal geometry with sp³d³ hybridization?
questions.explanation: Iodine heptafluoride (IF₇) has 7 single bonds and zero lone pairs, giving a regular pentagonal bipyramidal geometry.

questions.question: Which noble gas produces a brilliant reddish-orange glow in discharge tubes and advertising signs?
questions.explanation: Neon discharge tubes emit intense red-orange light widely utilized in neon advertising signs.

questions.question: Why cannot fluorine form interhalogen compounds where it acts as the central atom (e.g., FCl₃ or FBr₅)?

options.B: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and lacks vacant d-orbitals in its n=2 shell to expand its octet

questions.explanation: Fluorine cannot accommodate more than 8 valence electrons due to the absence of 2d orbitals and is never positive relative to any other halogen.

questions.question: What is the molecular geometry of Chlorine trifluoride (ClF₃)?
questions.explanation: ClF₃ has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (sp³d). Lone pairs occupy equatorial sites, yielding a slightly bent T-shaped molecule.

questions.question: Which noble gas was the first to be synthesized into a true chemical compound (Xe⁺[PtF₆]⁻) by Neil Bartlett in 1962?
questions.explanation: Bartlett observed that PtF₆ oxidized O₂ to O₂⁺; recognizing that Xenon's first IE (1170 kJ/mol) was nearly identical to O₂ (1175 kJ/mol), he synthesized XePtF₆.

questions.question: Which halogen sublimes directly from a dark purple crystalline solid into violet vapors upon heating?
questions.explanation: Solid iodine has a high vapor pressure and sublimes easily at mild temperatures to generate rich violet fumes.

questions.question: Tincture of iodine, a classic antiseptic solution, contains:

options.B: 2-3% solution of Iodine and Potassium Iodide (KI) in an alcohol-water mixture

questions.explanation: Tincture of iodine is 2-3% I₂ with KI dissolved in ethanol-water; KI enhances iodine solubility via formation of soluble triiodide ions (I₃⁻).

questions.question: Which of the following halogens is a fuming, dark reddish-brown liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Bromine is the only non-metallic element that exists as a liquid under standard temperature and pressure.

questions.question: What is the geometry of Xenon trioxide (XeO₃)?
questions.explanation: XeO₃ has 3 Xe=O double bonds and one lone pair on Xenon (sp³), producing a trigonal pyramidal structure similar to ammonia.

questions.question: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) is stored in wax-coated bottles or plastic (polyethylene) containers because:

options.A: It reacts with glass (silica) forming soluble fluorosilicic acid: SiO₂ + 6HF → H₂SiF₆ + 2H₂O
options.B: It is light-sensitive and decomposes into fluorine gas
options.D: It oxidizes glass into silicon metal

questions.explanation: HF attacks silicates in glass (etching of glass), forming gaseous SiF₄ and H₂SiF₆, destroying glass containers.

questions.question: Which of the following ions produces an intense deep-blue complex with starch solution?
questions.explanation: Polyiodide chains (I₅⁻ / I₃⁻) insert into the amylose helix of starch, producing an intense charge-transfer blue color.

questions.question: The most abundant noble gas present in Earth's dry atmosphere (approximately 0.93% by volume) is:
questions.explanation: Argon constitutes ~0.934% of air, accumulating over geological time through the radioactive decay of Potassium-40 in rocks.

questions.question: What happens when chlorine water is exposed to sunlight for a few hours?

options.B: It loses its yellowish-green color and liberates oxygen gas: 2 Cl₂ + 2 H₂O xrightarrow{hν} 4 HCl + O₂↑

questions.explanation: In sunlight, unstable HOCl in chlorine water photolyzes: 2 HOCl → 2 HCl + O₂↑, releasing oxygen and leaving dilute HCl.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is known as 'Freon-12' and was historically used as an aerosol propellant and refrigerant?
questions.explanation: Dichlorodifluoromethane (CF₂Cl₂) is designated Freon-12 (CFC-12).

questions.question: What is the oxidation state of iodine in periodic acid (HIO₄ / H₅IO₆)?
questions.explanation: In metaperiodic acid (HIO₄) or paraperiodic acid (H₅IO₆), iodine exhibits its maximum oxidation state of +7.

questions.question: Which halogen displacement reaction will occur spontaneously?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is more electronegative with higher reduction potential than bromine, easily displacing bromide from aqueous KBr.

questions.question: What is the hybridization of Xenon in Xenon hexafluoride (XeF₆)?
questions.explanation: XeF₆ has 6 bond pairs and 1 stereochemically active lone pair (steric number 7 = sp³d³), giving a distorted octahedral geometry.

questions.question: Argon gas is filled inside incandescent filament lamps primarily to:

options.B: Provide an inert atmosphere that inhibits evaporation and burning of the tungsten filament

questions.explanation: Chemically inert argon suppresses tungsten vaporization at high operating temperatures (~2500°C), prolonging lamp life.

questions.question: Which of the following hydrogen halides does not precipitate silver halide upon adding aqueous silver nitrate (AgNO₃)?
questions.explanation: Silver fluoride (AgF) is water-soluble, whereas AgCl (white), AgBr (cream), and AgI (yellow) are insoluble precipitates.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is used as a tear gas (lachrymator) in riot control?
questions.explanation: Chloropicrin (trichloronitromethane, CCl₃NO₂) severely irritates mucus membranes and induces uncontrollable tearing.

questions.question: The boiling points of the noble gases increase steadily down the group from Helium to Radon because:

options.B: Increasing polarizability and electron count lead to stronger London dispersion forces

questions.explanation: Larger electron clouds are more easily distorted, leading to stronger instantaneous dipole-induced dipole (London dispersion) forces.

questions.question: In the reaction of Xenon with fluorine at 400°C and 1 atmosphere pressure in a nickel vessel (1:5 volume ratio), the major product is:
questions.explanation: Heating Xe and F₂ in a 1:5 ratio at 400°C and 1 atm yields crystalline Xenon tetrafluoride (XeF₄).

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a 'pseudo-halogen'?
questions.explanation: Cyanogen [(CN)₂] consists of electronegative groups that mimic halogens in forming pseudohalide ions (CN⁻) and covalent interhalogens (ICN).

questions.question: Bleaching action of chlorine gas in the presence of moisture is due to:

options.B: Oxidation of colored matter by nascent oxygen released from hypochlorous acid (HOCl)

questions.explanation: Cl₂ + H₂O ⇌ HCl + HOCl; HOCl → HCl + [O]. Nascent oxygen permanently bleaches dyes by oxidation.
